title: Regional Alert Curation and Surgical Load-Shedding Runbook
creator: Asha Rao
description:
Summary:
This ticket implements an operational layer — the Alert Curation + Surgical Shedding Orchestrator — to reduce noisy pages while preserving high-fidelity SLO-driven failover. The goal is to give on-call engineers deterministic, low-friction runbook actions for regional degradations and to automate the first-response mitigation (circuit thresholds, staged shedding, KV-cache bypassing) for common failure modes.

Motivation & Goals:
- Reduce high-volume, low-actionable alerts during short-lived regional degradations by 50% in Q2 while keeping pager latency for high-severity incidents <= 1 min.
- Implement deterministic load-shedding policies per region (grace and shed windows) coupled to SLO burn-rate and circuit state.
- Provide a well-documented, testable on-call runbook that can be executed manually or by Runbook Runner (automation) with safe rollback and canary behaviors.
- Ensure the system is auditable (linkable events in audit logs) and reversible without code deploys.

Design Overview:
1) Telemetry scoring layer (Alert Curation):
   - Normalize signals across metrics (error-rate, p50/p95 latency, queue-depth, GPU-util) into a single regional "event score" (0-100).
   - Apply signal-weight multipliers based on customer-impact label and route (control-plane vs. inference).
   - Use sliding windows: burst-window 30s, persistence-window 10m to reduce noisy transient alerts.

2) Staged circuit & shedding controller:
   - Circuit states: CLOSED -> MONITORING -> SOFT-TRIP -> HARD-TRIP -> DEGRADING -> RECOVERING.
   - Soft-trips apply conservative shedding (0-10% of requests; preferentially low-cost/cached traffic).
   - Hard-trips invoke aggressive shedding (20-60%) and model variant fallback routing to other regions or cheaper model variant with lower latency guarantees.
   - All trips are gated by SLO burn-rate threshold (>3x projected burn within 30m) and capacity signals.

3) Runbook model & automated play executor:
   - Human-readable playbook segments for each circuit state with exact commands, dashboards, and expected outcomes.
   - Runbook Runner hooks: a) dry-run, b) pre-checks (dependency, capacity), c) execute (API calls to router/circuit controller), d) post-check and audit event.
   - Safety interlocks: require manual confirmation to exceed 30% shedding for first 3 weeks after rollout.

4) Observability & feedback:
   - New dashboards: regional-event-score, shedding-impact, route-fallback-latency, oncall-action-log.
   - Synthetic canary probes for each region to validate recovery and ensure shedding isn't masking total outage.

Tradeoffs considered:
- Aggressive dedupe vs. missing a novel failure mode: we choose conservative dedupe parameters (30s burst window) and keep rules editable per route.
- Automated remediation vs. noisy flapping: gated automation with cool-downs and circuit hysteresis prevents oscillation.
- Shedding accuracy vs. complexity: favor simple, deterministic percent-based shedding initially; refine by route over time.

Implementation Plan (Milestones):
- Week 1: Telemetry scoring prototype + local simulator. Metrics: precision/recall of labeled incidents. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4897)
- Week 2: Circuit controller + staged shedding API + runbook DSL. Integrate with router service. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-router/pull/2123)
- Week 3: Deploy in staging multi-region test, run failure injection (packet loss, GPU OOM, model stall) and verify non-flapping behavior. (Dashboard: grafana.redwood.internal/d/alert-curation)
- Week 4: Canary rollout to low-traffic customers in eu-west-1 with manual approval gating. Collect metrics for 7 days.
- Week 6: Full rollout with automated runbook Runner enabled for SOFT-TRIP actions; manual confirmation still required for HARD-TRIP >30% shedding.

Runbook (excerpt — to be published to Confluence):
- Detect: If regional-event-score > 55 for > 5m and p95 latency increased > 2x -> escalate to MONITORING.
- Verify: Check api-500-rate, model-queue-depth, GPU-util. Run synthetic probes.
- Mitigate (SOFT-TRIP): Invoke /v1/orchestrator/shed?region=<r>&percent=8&route=lowest-priority; runbook-runner executes dry-run then apply; wait 3 minutes and verify p95.
- If event-score persists > 70 and SLO burn-rate > 3x -> escalate to HARD-TRIP: shed 30% and enable cross-region fallback for critical routes.
- Notify: Post to #oncall-ops with tags region, circuit-state, shedding-percent, and link to runbook and incident channel.
- Recover: When event-score < 25 for 15m and synthetic probes pass, gradually recover shedding by 10% increments with 5m observation windows.
- Postmortem: If shedding invoked, require an incident note describing root cause hypothesis and whether shedding prevented customer-visible errors.

Safety, Auditing, and Compliance:
- All shedding actions produce an immutable audit event with actor (human or automation), before/after state, and links to PRs/dashboards.
- RBAC: Only SRE rotation members can trigger HARD-TRIP without offline approval; automation service account limited to SOFT-TRIP actions.

Acceptance Criteria:
- 50% reduction in low-actionable pages for the targeted routes over a 30-day window in canary region.
- No false-positive HARD-TRIP events during chaos-run experiments (runbook simulator pass rate >= 95%).
- SREs report runbook clarity score >= 4/5 in internal survey after 2 weeks.
